(2) Carters Price Guide lots 857946 ('A Georgian sterling silver pepperette, 1784 London') and 1151508 ('Four various antique sterling silver pepperettes'): no price was ever seen; I retried curl and got HTTP 403 again, so they are leads only for a person to open, not evidence. Web search budget was exhausted for this run, so no new comparables could be found; a follow-up search (Leonard Joel, Lawsons, Theodore Bruce, Invaluable, Gowans past results) is needed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged photo 3: lid rim carries a lion passant and a capital R, so the lid is marked and matches the body. Body carries a lion passant (the researcher read this as a maker mark), a crowned leopard's head (London), a capital Roman R in a shaped shield, and a partly visible fourth mark that could be the sovereign's head duty mark or the maker's mark; no maker mark is legible. In my reading of the London cycles, 1776-95 used lowercase letters (1792 = lowercase r) and 1796-1815 used capitals, so a capital R suggests 1812-13 rather than the researcher's 1792; not checked against a hallmark table. Either way it is George III. Urn body, domed pierced cover, square foot, monogram MH, gilt interior with some wear, general tarnish and light surface wear, no obvious split or large dent visible in 4 photos.
lots.condition: Appears sound from 4 photos: tarnish, light scratches, gilt interior worn in places, piercing intact. Dents or repairs at the foot or seam cannot be ruled out. Weight not stated.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm the weight, whether there is a maker's mark and what the fourth body mark is (duty head or maker), whether the cover fits firmly, and whether there are any dents, splits or repairs to the stem, foot or seam?
